intent.purpose: Accumulate operational learning across sessions — observations, insights, patterns, and proposals that feed future session intelligence prep, framework evolution, and harness improvement. The institutional memory for this project. Adapted from CALL (Center for Army Lessons Learned) institutional database pattern: individual sessions produce observations, this file synthesizes them into insights and proposals that persist
intent.scope: Cross-session learning only. Observations citing session estimates, insights connecting observations across sessions, patterns that generalize, proposals with barrier analysis, carry-forward gap tracking, governed vocabulary findings. NOT session operational state (main running estimate). NOT incident tracking (incidents.json via /incident). NOT framework registry data (framework-registry.json via /frameworks). NOT fix specifications (those come from plans)

observations.observation: The carry-forward pipeline has a structural gap: code changes (committed during session by agent) carry forward via git. SessionEnd hook outputs (harvesting artifacts, session archives) do NOT — they're produced after the last commit and stranded on the local machine
observations.evidence: v0.63.0 commit contains only running-estimate.json + RELEASE_NOTES.md. session-archive.sh:11 explicitly says 'No git operations.' harvest-session.sh has no git operations. harvesting/ on Windows stops at 3/19; Mac has artifacts through 3/22. Decision #1 proposes auto-commit/push but is NOT implemented

observations.observation: Cross-platform hook failures are a recurring pattern (4th instance): $MODE unset (v0.29.2), find -printf GNU-only (v0.31.0), Stop hook type wrong (bc2429e), stat -f BSD-only (this session). Each time: written on macOS, tested on macOS, deployed to both platforms, discovered broken on Windows
observations.evidence: git log commits 6427f53, 7b4033e, bc2429e. Current stat -f crash reproduced empirically. All hook commits say '(tested: macOS)'. No check script validates hook cross-platform portability

observations.observation: Correct patterns exist in the codebase but new code uses old patterns. get_mtime() extracted into check-lib.sh (v0.32.0). session-archive.sh uses uname -s dispatch. But hooks written AFTER these extractions used the old broken stat -f || stat -c pattern
observations.evidence: check-lib.sh:162 (get_mtime), session-archive.sh:68 (uname dispatch) — both correct. surfacing-duty-stop.sh:53, estimate-refresh-stop.sh:111 — both broken, written later

observations.observation: The governed vocabulary enforces observation precision. Overclaims ('every Windows turn,' 'carry-forward is blocked,' '3rd instance') were caught when audited against governed definitions. The observation-to-fact pipeline (observe → classify → verify → correct) ran 3 passes in this session, each catching errors the previous missed
observations.evidence: O78 (wrong carry-forward claim corrected), F9 (3rd→4th instance corrected), AS7 (overclaim downgraded to assumption), O44 (search expanded from 1 to 30 terms)

observations.observation: Search breadth determines discovery quality. One search term ('unbound') found 0 commits. Thirty terms across 2 repos found 64+ commits including the exact prior art (commit 6427f53). The narrow search produced a false negative ('no prior art exists') that broader search corrected
observations.evidence: O44 (original narrow search), O85 (expanded search results)

observations.observation: Platform transitions require Lagebeurteilung before resuming prior Schwerpunkt. The prior session set accepting Schwerpunkt to 'Build channel infrastructure.' Switching to Windows revealed 3 failure clusters that the prior session (Mac-only) couldn't have known about. The Schwerpunkt had to shift to platform stabilization
observations.evidence: Running estimate v7 acceptingSessionSchwerpunkt vs v8 Schwerpunkt. Prior session ran 28 delegations on Mac with no Windows testing

observations.observation: The hooks directory contains both correct and incorrect cross-platform patterns side by side. session-archive.sh (correct uname dispatch) and surfacing-duty-stop.sh (broken stat -f) are in the same shared/hooks/ directory. No code review or check script caught the inconsistency
observations.evidence: session-archive.sh:68 vs surfacing-duty-stop.sh:53. Same directory, different patterns, no enforcement

observations.observation: The namespace consolidation (decision #34: .scratch/ → .aitools/scratch/, harvesting/ → .aitools/harvesting/) has NOT been implemented in the hooks. harvest-session.sh references .scratch/ and harvesting/ at repo root. The hooks and the workspace rule are out of sync
observations.evidence: harvest-session.sh:35 ($PROJECT_ROOT/.scratch), harvest-session.sh:49 ($PROJECT_ROOT/harvesting). Workspace rule (.claude/rules/aitools-workspace.md) specifies .aitools/ paths

observations.observation: The Deploy-Configs function suppresses all output (*> $null 2>> $logFile), creating silent failures in reusable code — violating USO. When 6 deploy scripts crashed, zero diagnostic output reached the log. Prior bugs in the same function (commit 682be4d: $LASTEXITCODE false positives) show this is a recurring fragility surface
observations.evidence: aitools.ps1:318 (*> $null pattern), deploy.log (zero stderr between build completion and error entries), commit 682be4d (prior bugs)

insights.insight: The harness has a gap where SessionEnd hook outputs are produced but never committed (we call this the 'commit gap' — ungoverned term, see vocabularyFindings). The carry-forward mechanism (git tracked files) works. The running estimate proved it — committed during session, pulled on Windows, carried forward. The gap is that SessionEnd hook outputs are never committed. Decision #1 (auto-commit/push) is the designed fix but hasn't been implemented across 6 sessions since it was decided. This is the highest-priority pipeline fix because every session that ends without it loses harvested artifacts and session archives

Cross-platform failures repeat because there is no DETECTION layer for platform portability. The PREVENTION layer exists (cross-platform.md rule, correct patterns in check-lib.sh). The AUDIT layer exists (/compat skill proposed). But no hook or check script catches platform-specific commands in hooks before deployment. Per three-layer governance, the missing layer is where failures persist

Governed vocabulary is not documentation — it is an active quality gate. Without it, the running estimate contains overclaims, ambiguities, and assumptions disguised as facts. The same dynamic that caused the v4 false .gitignore claim (prior session) would have recurred in v8 if the vocabulary hadn't forced classification. The observation-to-fact pipeline IS the quality mechanism

The workspace is in a TRANSITION state. Decisions #34 (namespace consolidation) and D-PER-SESSION-ESTIMATES (per-session estimates) are decided but not implemented ON WINDOWS. The Mac may have progressed further. Commander explicitly stated 'most of where stuff lives and naming conventions are assumptions.' Any assumption about structure, paths, or naming on this Windows clone is an assumption, not a fact

The harness needs a CONFIGURATION AUDIT mechanism for cross-machine state. When work happens on one machine and isn't fully committed, the other machine's running estimate, planning brief, and architectural assumptions diverge silently. The divergence is invisible until someone switches machines. ISO 10007 (configuration status accounting) and IPB (intelligence gaps with collection plans) both address this: document the baseline, track changes, audit divergences. The running estimate's carryForwardGaps section is a start but lacks the confidence dimension — we need VERIFIED/STALE/SUPERSEDED/UNKNOWN per item

The user model is broader than any single session captures. aitools users span: single-platform, multi-platform, single-user, multi-user collaborating, working on aitools itself, or only using aitools on other projects. Design decisions that assume single-user-multi-machine (the current dominant pattern) may not hold for multi-user scenarios. The dashboard, channel, and concurrency architectures must account for all combinations. This was understood on the Mac session but not documented in the repo
insights.framework: Mission command (user model), Platform engineering (multi-platform support)

patterns.description: Code written and tested on one platform, deployed to both, discovered broken on the other. Has occurred 4 times for hooks. Also applies to dotprofile CLAUDE.md template (incident #28). The prevention is platform-aware validation before deployment, not post-deployment discovery
patterns.structuralFix: Decision #8 (Platform engineering framework) with detection-layer hook for portability checking

patterns.pattern: Correct pattern exists but new code uses old pattern
patterns.description: A correct solution is extracted/documented (get_mtime, uname dispatch, deploy_managed_file) but subsequent code written after the extraction uses the pre-extraction pattern. The extraction provides the capability but not the enforcement
patterns.structuralFix: Check script that greps for known-bad patterns in registered all-platform scripts (decision #8 component 8)

patterns.description: During-session code changes get committed (agent makes git commits). End-of-session hook outputs do not (no git operations in hooks). The commit is SELECTIVE — intentional artifacts committed, hook-produced artifacts stranded. Repeats every session until decision #1 is implemented

Work done on one machine creates decisions, artifacts, and architectural changes that are not fully committed/pushed. The other machine operates on a stale baseline, treating old decisions as current. The divergence is invisible until someone switches machines and does a Lagebeurteilung. From configuration management (ISO 10007): this is a configuration baseline divergence requiring a configuration audit

patterns.pattern: OL is everywhere, not a silo
patterns.description: Operational learning is not a standalone artifact — it's a layer that attaches to every harness activity. Sessions, mission command, delegation, artifacts, frameworks, provenance, channels all produce and consume learning. Across all provenance (CALL institutional, Deming embedded, Argyris double-loop, SRE event-driven, safety engineering contextual): learning is embedded in the process, accumulated across events, and applied continuously. A separate OL file captures the SYNTHESIS but not the learning itself — the learning happens everywhere

proposals.proposal: Implement decision #1 (auto-commit/push) as the highest-priority pipeline fix. Every session without it loses harvested artifacts and session archives. The running estimate proved carry-forward works when committed — extend to all SessionEnd outputs
proposals.barrierAnalysis: If decision #1 had been implemented before session 5HyCwPtSDH: harvesting artifacts from 3/20-3/22 would be on Windows now. Session archives in dotprofile would be committed. The 'stale by 3 days' observation would not exist. PASSES barrier test

proposals.proposal: Add a hook portability check to the pre-commit or post-push check scripts. Grep all registered hooks for known-bad patterns (stat -f, find -printf, grep -P, date -d) and flag them. This is the missing detection layer
proposals.barrierAnalysis: If a portability check existed before the stop hooks were committed: the stat -f pattern would have been flagged. The hook would have been written with uname dispatch from the start. PASSES barrier test for OL-O2, OL-O3, OL-O7
